meaning: Half of the donkeys in the plunder from Midian—allocated respectively to the warriors and the congregation
description: The number 30500 appears twice in Numbers 31, as half of the total 61000 donkeys that the Israelites took as war spoils after their victory over the Midianites. The war was waged at the Lord's command as retribution for Midian's seduction of Israel at Peor. In accordance with God's ordinance, the war spoils were divided into two equal parts: 30500 donkeys for the warriors who had taken part in the battle (v. 39), and 30500 donkeys for the rest of the congregation (v. 45). From the warriors' share, a tribute to the Lord was calculated as one out of every five hundred, that is, 61 donkeys which were given to the high priest Eleazar. From the congregation's share, one out of fifty was given to the Levites, that is, 610 donkeys. This precise and symmetrical distribution shows that all war spoils ultimately belonged to God, and that the division followed an ordered, divine system in which priests, Levites, soldiers, and the people each received their rightful portion.

versions.meaning: Number of donkeys in the plunder from Midian
versions.description: The number 30500 appears in Numbers 31 as the total count of donkeys the Israelites took as war spoils after their victory over the Midianites. This war was carried out at the Lord's command as retribution for Midian's seduction of Israel at Peor. Of the 30500 donkeys, half (15250) were given to the warriors who had taken part in the battle, and the other half was given to the rest of the congregation. From the warriors' share, a tribute was calculated for the Lord: one out of every five hundred, which amounted to 61 donkeys as the Lord's portion. From the congregation's share, one out of fifty was given to the Levites. This precise accounting shows that all war spoils ultimately belonged to God, and that the distribution followed an orderly, divine system in which priests, Levites, soldiers, and the people each received their share.

footnotes.text: The war against Midian in Numbers 31 was ordered as punishment for the role of the Midianites in the Baal-Peor incident (Num 25), where Israel was led into idolatry and immorality.

The tax system in Numbers 31 operates with two rates: one five-hundredth of the warriors' half went to the high priest as a "gift to the Lord," while one fiftieth of the congregation's half went to the Levites who served at the tabernacle.
The total plunder included 675,000 sheep, 72,000 cattle, 61,000 donkeys, and 32,000 young women—an enumeration that underscores thorough record-keeping and God's sovereignty over all outcomes of war.

footnotes.text: The war against Midian in Numbers 31 was ordered as punishment for the role of the Midianites in the Baal-Peor incident (Num 25), where Israel was led into idolatry and immorality.

The tax system in Numbers 31 operates with two rates: one five-hundredth of the warriors' half went to the high priest as a "gift to the Lord," while one fiftieth of the congregation's half went to the Levites who served at the tabernacle.
